ca_arch_angel_amphitheater_crooked_piton.descent_text: From the top of the last pitch, hike down to the Devil's Slide trail, which returns to Humber Park.

ca_hinterland_corridor_breathing_space.approach: Go high up the Hinterland Gully to the south side of its left flank; the climb starts in a left-facing corner, at the same start as Ridgeback.

ca_hinterland_wall_aquarium.approach: The route is on the far left side of Hinterland Wall and begins in a left-facing dihedral.

ca_hinterland_wall_natural_mystic.approach: The route is on Hinterland Wall and shares its first-pitch dihedral start with the route Aquarium, at the far left side of the wall.

ca_long_buttress_devil_s_snare.descent_text: The climbs on this buttress are gear-only and the descent is a walk-off.

ca_long_buttress_magic_staircase.descent_text: Build a gear belay at the top of the second pitch and walk off.

ca_north_face_the_marmotzilla.descent_text: Head left to the ridge from the top of the corner and scramble down to climber's left.

ca_north_face_the_nazg_l.descent_text: The route reaches the northeast ridge; one finish traverses left to the ridge, from where parties scramble off to climber's left.

ca_regge_pole_free_radical.approach: Talus below the tower scrambles easily to its foot, and the route begins right at the toe.

ca_seven_gables_7th_gable_or_spiral_ridg.approach: From the east, begin at the Pine Creek Pass trailhead and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail beyond Upper Pine Lake, branching toward Honeymoon Lake. Carry on through Granite Park to the crest, which you cross at Granite Bear Pass, south of Italy Pass beside Granite Park Spire. Go west cross-country into the Bear Lakes area, passing Big Bear Lake on its north and Little Bear Lake on its south, then trend southwest past tarns to Vee Lake. Walk down its outlet to the East Fork of Bear Creek and work uphill cross-country to the peak. The route is the leftmost gable on the north face.

ca_sky_blue_diamond_altared_state.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, over New or Old Army Pass, or over Arc Pass, with good camping anywhere along the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond is the steep, clean, diamond-shaped shield due south of Sky Blue Lake: counting from the far left, it is the fourth of the walls and towers leading up to the lake. Altared State is right of the A-frame crack that splits the headwall and follows a clean right-facing crack system across the shield. From the base, scramble to a broad ledge running across the formation's right side; a brief fourth-class step guards access to it.
ca_sky_blue_diamond_altared_state.descent_text: A huge ledge below the summit can be walked off to the right (north), and non-technical terrain leads all the way back to the base. From the summit, reverse the route down to that ledge by downclimbing and a couple of rappels; the summit block itself has a low fifth-class move to reverse.

ca_sky_blue_diamond_stupa_troopers.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, over New or Old Army Pass, or over Arc Pass, with good camping anywhere along the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond is the steep, clean, diamond-shaped shield due south of Sky Blue Lake: counting from the far left, it is the fourth of the walls and towers leading up to the lake. Stupa Troopers is just left of Altared State and climbs the whole shield by sustained cracks, starting with a short pitch that has a few pitons in an incipient crack.
ca_sky_blue_diamond_stupa_troopers.descent_text: A huge ledge below the summit can be walked off to the right (north), and non-technical terrain leads back to the base. From the summit, reverse the route to that ledge by downclimbing and a couple of rappels.

ca_sky_blue_diamond_journey_to_the_cente.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, over New or Old Army Pass, or over Arc Pass, with good camping anywhere along the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond is the steep, clean, diamond-shaped shield due south of Sky Blue Lake: counting from the far left, it is the fourth of the walls and towers leading up to the lake. Journey to the Center of the Earth follows one long splitter crack through the middle of the Diamond's tallest section, entering the left side of the big alcove roughly two-thirds of the way up and climbing through it.

ca_sky_blue_diamond_spankin_the_marmot_a.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, over New or Old Army Pass, or over Arc Pass, with good camping anywhere along the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond is the steep, clean, diamond-shaped shield due south of Sky Blue Lake: counting from the far left, it is the fourth of the walls and towers leading up to the lake. Spankin' the Marmot sits at the left end of the Diamond, on a tidy vertical splitter that bends left into a tall dihedral. The first section is a scramble up stepped ledges and corners to the foot of the headwall, with access from the far-left gully.

ca_southern_cross_clean_living.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Clean Living begins on a vertical crack system about midway between Taphophobia and Fear of Flying, on the gently overhanging orange face.

ca_southern_cross_pure_thoughts.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Pure Thoughts begins from a belay in the Taphophobia corner and steps right onto flakes on the gently overhanging face.

ca_southern_cross_fear_of_fun_aka_southe.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Fear of Fun starts a short way left of The Astraphobia Treatment and joins it higher up.

ca_southern_cross_delta_crucis.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Delta Crucis is on the southwest face and is one of the westernmost full-length routes, around the corner to the right of The Astraphobia Treatment, and lower on the hillside than the short route that climbs the pillar farther right. It begins in the white groove and aims for the right side of the big headwall.

ca_sphinx_the_northeast_ridge.approach: Pull off on the outer edge of Tioga Road right under the formation and climb the shattered slabs above the road to the base, or start from the Warren Creek trailhead at the unofficial campground on the bend in US 120. The line follows the east ridge, which can be joined at the saddle reached from the back side, or traversed in full from Warren Creek, a loose option.

ca_spring_lake_wall_spring_roll.approach: The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake. The wall rises directly above the lake near the head of Cliff Creek Canyon and is split into three buttresses. Spring Roll takes the leftmost of the three formations, starting at its toe up a right-facing layback corner.
ca_spring_lake_wall_spring_roll.descent_text: Go left over the back of the formation toward Cyclamen Lake; a steep gully on the way may need a short rappel from a slung boulder. Keep angling left and down the slabs to return to Spring Lake. Alternatively, go on to the top of the main formation and use its descent.

ca_the_fortress_2_the_sage.approach: In Sequoia National Park, start up the Paradise Ridge trail from the trailhead by Atwell Mill campground, along the Mineral King road, and climb it to the ridge. Leave the trail there and travel cross-country north-northwest, contouring across small drainages, until the wall and the gully beneath it appear. Keep to the gully's east side until you are under the wall, then cross over and go up to the base. The Sage is on the south face. From the bivy site, work left around the wall and slightly upward over dirt ledges to the foot of the first left-facing corner, which lies down and right of the large corner where the pillar joins the main face.

ca_tuttle_south_basecamp_wall_basecamp_h.approach: Take the Tuttle Creek trail to the Ashram, then turn left onto a sandy sidehill path that reaches the South Fork of Tuttle Creek, and go up the drainage, looking for cairns. When the ground is clear of snow, keep north of the creek for more than half the distance, passing Keyhole Wall on your right, and cross at a meadow; with snow, cross to the south side sooner. Stay with the creek until it runs directly under the wall, below the Obelisk. Basecamp Hearsay starts at the foot of the long squeeze chimney inside the big dihedral, the dominant feature of the wall.

ca_upper_brownstone_alpine_creek.approach: Keep climbing the Pine Creek trail until the wall shows on your left, then work up the basin below it along its right-hand side. Alpine Creek starts on the right side of the triangular slab.

ca_upper_brownstone_thinking_makes_it_so.approach: Keep climbing the Pine Creek trail until the wall shows on your left, then work up the basin below it along its right-hand side. Thinking Makes It So begins on a pedestal at the buttress toe, to the left of the slab.

co_choice_s_buttress_timeless_visons.descent_text: Walk off around to the west.

co_glen_cove_crack_shack_crack_thief.descent_text: Either rappel to the west from just below the ledge using the tat and ring there, or scramble up the broken ground above and walk down Big Blue.

co_southeast_face_coming_of_age.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right via obvious grassy ledges, with perhaps a fourth-class move or two.

co_the_citadel_2_tempest.descent_text: Rappel the route itself, or use the chains at the top to make one rappel down the tower's north face.

co_the_citadel_2_tempest_in_a_teapot.descent_text: Descend as for Tempest: rappel the route, or take the chains at the top for a rappel down the tower's north face.

co_the_stargate_the_eye_of_ra.descent_text: Go down the avalanche chute on the buttress's east side, which faces north, to reach the valley. The chute is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
co_the_stargate_the_eye_of_ra.approach: This is a far-off north-facing buttress in the valley south of the Walk of Life Spire. Begin at the pond and meadow under the spire's scree field and follow the side valley that branches south, right to the foot of the Stargate. The route climbs the weakness just left of the centre of the buttress.

mt_smash_n_grab_slab_the_tee_time.descent_text: From the top walk up a little, then traverse hard left back to the Oberlin climbers trail, which leads to the parking lot.

nh_alpine_breeze_wall_route_66.descent_text: Rappel from the two-bolt anchor on top of the buttress.

qc_la_grande_dalle_distanciation_sociale.descent_text: Descent is by rappel down the route, or by the hiking trail marked with orange ribbons.

wy_boy_scout_cirque_route_list_where_s_b.descent_text: Descend by rappel from the sling anchors at the top of the climb.

wy_cathedral_buttress_the_widowmaker.descent_text: Descend by the Snaz walk-off: the descent chimneys and gully to the south of the buttress.
